news.title: AI Weekly: SpaceX's huge AI spend, Anthropic's hack scare
news.summary:
STORY: From to investor worries over SpaceX AI spend to Anthropic's hacking scare ...

This is AI Weekly.

:: AI Weekly

SpaceX said it saw faster-than-expected returns from its AI spending in its first-ever earnings call as a public company.

But investors were still worried about how long its Starlink business can continue to bankroll costly investments in data centers and Nvidia chips, and shares dropped 12%.

Quarterly capital spending on AI climbed to $15.8 billion.

The company said the economics of its investments were quickly improving, but signaled AI spending would stay elevated.

Anthropic said some of its Claude AI models hacked into the systems of three companies during cybersecurity tests.

It came days after rival OpenAI revealed one of its AI agents also went on a rogue attack.

The new incidents were due to a mistake which accidentally gave Anthropic's models access to the open internet.

OpenAI's agent in contrast independently exploited a vulnerability to reach the internet during cyber testing.

Samsung posted a 250-fold jump in chip profit of $61.7 billion for the second quarter.

The world's biggest memory chipmaker also said it believes its chip shortage will run through to 2028.

But the bullish outlook didn't calm investor concerns on how AI infrastructure spending could curb growth for tech firms.

AI kept the U.S. economy growing even as overall expansion slowed down.

The so-called advance reading from the Commerce Department showed gross domestic product rose 1.5% - below economist forecasts.

But AI-related spending kept domestic demand high.

Business spending on equipment jumped more than 15%, generating a second straight quarter of double digit growth.
